title: Season 2, Ep 7: The enterprise evaluation platform
oneliner: Evaluate LLM output systematically: an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline, curated datasets with ideal answers, and semantic regression tests in CI - so quality is measured, not vibes.
says: A critical task in any GenAI or agent project is evaluating the LLM's output. The platform answer: build an automated pipeline using LLM-as-a-judge architecture; use curated datasets with ideal outputs; and run semantic regression tests in the continuous integration pipeline. That is how you evaluate the LLM properly and serve the teams building agent projects.
explained: Evaluation is the least glamorous and most decisive platform service. Without it, every model upgrade, prompt change, or SDK update is a leap of faith - quality drifts and nobody notices until users complain. His three pieces form the fix. Curated datasets are the exam: real questions with ideal answers, owned by people who know the domain. LLM-as-a-judge is the grader: a strong model scoring the candidate model's answers against the ideals, which scales where human review cannot.

Semantic regression testing in CI is the enforcement: every change gets graded before it ships, and a score drop fails the build - the exact moment where the Guardrails-as-Code reel becomes real. Together these convert 'we think the assistant got worse' into a number with a history, which is what lets a platform team approve changes across dozens of LOBs without reading every response.
takeaway: Quality needs infrastructure: golden datasets, an LLM judge, and CI gates that fail on regression. Without them you are shipping on vibes.
